To preview issues that the rest of the book will explore.
To replace the earlier definition with a financial one.
To demonstrate that no research on richness exists.

questions.passage: Happiness is the ultimate goal of goals, according to Aristotle.
questions.prompt: Who is explicitly associated with the idea that happiness is “the ultimate goal of goals”?
options: William James.
Aristotle.
Ed Diener.
The survey respondents.
analyses: A James 出现在下一句，不是这句 ultimate goal 的归属。
B according to Aristotle 明示归属。
C Diener 与后面的国际调查相关。
D 调查对象提供重视程度，不是该表述的署名来源。

evidence.quote: Happiness is the ultimate goal of goals, according to Aristotle.

questions.passage: The irony is that our blind pursuit of happiness sometimes leads to unhappiness. We put undue pressure and stress on ourselves to always be happy, preventing ourselves from reaping the benefits.
questions.prompt: What irony introduces the discussion of the happiness trap?
options: No one sees happiness as a worthwhile goal.
Happy people never help others.
Pursuing happiness blindly can sometimes produce unhappiness.
Public happiness always reflects inner experience.
analyses: A 先前称 worthy goal，并非所有人否定。
B 与前文 more prosocial 相反，且 never 绝对化。
C 保留 blind pursuit 与 sometimes 的限定。
D 后面 precisely 区分外在表现与内在感受。

evidence.quote: The irony is that our blind pursuit of happiness sometimes leads to unhappiness.

vocabulary.context: 要求自己总快乐所施加的过分压力
vocabulary.example: The deadline placed undue pressure on the team.

questions.passage: The irony is that our blind pursuit of happiness sometimes leads to unhappiness. We put undue pressure and stress on ourselves to always be happy, preventing ourselves from reaping the benefits.
questions.prompt: How can pressure to be happy become counterproductive, according to the sentence?
questions.promptZh: 根据本句，要求自己幸福的压力怎样会适得其反？
options: It makes every enjoyable activity medically harmful.
It can keep people from gaining the benefits they seek.
It removes the need for any social relationships.
It guarantees that all unhappy people become better workers.
optionsZh: 它使每种愉快活动都在医学上有害。
它可能妨碍人获得原本寻求的益处。
它消除了社会关系的必要性。
它保证所有不幸福的人都会成为更好的员工。
analyses: A 原文针对 undue pressure，不是所有愉快活动。
B preventing ourselves from reaping the benefits 说明过度施压妨碍获益。
C 没有说社会关系不再必要。
D better workers 属于前面的描述，不能移为压力的确定结果。

vocabulary.context: 修饰为了始终幸福而给自己的过度压力。
vocabulary.example: The deadline placed undue pressure on the small team.

questions.passage: Take Madison Holleran, a “popular, attractive, and talented” first-year student at the University of Pennsylvania. According to The New York Times, she “posted images that show her smiling, dappled in sunshine or kicking back at a party.” Her social media epitomized happiness. Yet her reality was more tenuous.
questions.prompt: How is Madison Holleran introduced in this passage?
questions.promptZh: 本段最初怎样介绍麦迪逊·霍勒兰？
options: As a first-year student at the University of Pennsylvania.
As a graduate researcher at the Centers for Disease Control.
As a teacher reporting on her former university students.
As a journalist conducting an international happiness survey.
optionsZh: 宾夕法尼亚大学一年级学生。
美国疾控中心的研究生研究人员。
讲述昔日大学学生经历的教师。
进行国际幸福调查的记者。
analyses: A first-year student at the University of Pennsylvania 明示身份和学校。
B CDC 是后文统计来源，不是她的身份；graduate 与 first-year 不符。
C 本句称她为学生，不是教师。
D 新闻报道和幸福调查是周围材料，不能把这些角色移给她。

vocabulary.context: Take Madison Holleran 让读者考虑这个案例，不是命令带走某个人。
vocabulary.example: Take public transport: a short journey can reveal many parts of a city.

questions.translation: 以 Madison Holleran 为例，她是宾夕法尼亚大学一名“受欢迎、外表出众且才华横溢”的一年级学生。据《纽约时报》报道，她“发布的照片中，自己或面带笑容，或沐浴在斑驳阳光里，或在聚会上放松休闲”。她的社交媒体俨然是幸福的典型写照。然而，她的现实生活却没有那么稳固。

evidence.quote: Take Madison Holleran, a “popular, attractive, and talented” first-year student at the University of Pennsylvania.

questions.passage: To her sister, she revealed feeling that her social life was inferior to that of her friends. On January 17, 2014, Madison jumped off the top of a parking garage and took her own life.
questions.prompt: In which year did the tragic event involving Madison occur, according to the passage?
questions.promptZh: 根据原文，麦迪逊遭遇的悲剧发生在哪一年？
analyses: A 2000 是后文统计区间起点，不是事件年份。
B 2018 出现在后文统计中，不能移到个人事件。
C On January 17, 2014 明确标明事件时间；本题核对时间信息。
D 2020 是后文另一组统计的年份，不是这里的日期。

vocabulary.meaning: 自杀身亡（对既往事件的中性表述）
vocabulary.context: 叙述已经发生的悲剧，不是美化表达，也不说明单一成因。
vocabulary.example: The report uses the phrase 'took her own life' when describing a past tragedy.
collocations: a report of a tragic death

questions.translation: 她向姐妹透露，觉得自己的社交生活不如朋友们。2014 年 1 月 17 日，Madison 从一座停车楼的顶部跳下，结束了自己的生命。

evidence.quote: On January 17, 2014, Madison jumped off the top of a parking garage and took her own life.

questions.passage: Suicide is an extremely complex behavior. Madison’s suicide must have been driven not just from feeling inferior to her friends’ social lives, but also from many other things. What is shocking is how good she was at pretending to be happy in public, and that a person who appeared so well adjusted and happy also had profound inner struggles leading to a tragic fate. Was she an exception or a rule?
questions.prompt: What does the author stress when discussing Madison’s death?
options: Social comparison alone fully explains it.
A cheerful appearance rules out serious inner difficulties.
Its complexity cannot be reduced to one feeling of inferiority.
Her private feelings were objectively identical to her friends’.
questions.promptZh: 作者讨论 Madison 的死亡时强调什么？
optionsZh: 仅凭社会比较就能完整解释。
快乐的外表能排除严重内心困扰。
其复杂性不能简化为一种自卑感。
她的私人感受客观上与朋友完全相同。
analyses: A not just...but also...明确拒绝单一因素解释。
B 原文恰好对照快乐表象与深刻内心挣扎。
C extremely complex 与 many other things 支持多因素、非单一解释。
D 没有对朋友感受作客观测量或等同判断。

evidence.quote: Suicide is an extremely complex behavior. Madison’s suicide must have been driven not just from feeling inferior to her friends’ social lives, but also from many other things.

vocabulary.context: 修饰内心挣扎，强调表象未呈现的深度
vocabulary.example: The journey had a profound effect on her outlook.

questions.translation: 自杀是一种极其复杂的行为。Madison 的自杀，驱动因素一定不只是觉得自己的社交生活不如朋友，还包括许多其他事情。令人震惊的是，她如此善于在公众面前装作快乐；一个看上去适应良好、很幸福的人，也有深刻的内心挣扎，最终走向悲剧。她是例外，还是普遍情形？

questions.passage: Suicide is an extremely complex behavior. Madison’s suicide must have been driven not just from feeling inferior to her friends’ social lives, but also from many other things. What is shocking is how good she was at pretending to be happy in public, and that a person who appeared so well adjusted and happy also had profound inner struggles leading to a tragic fate. Was she an exception or a rule?
questions.prompt: What contrast does the narrator find shocking in Madison's case?
questions.promptZh: 叙述者在麦迪逊的案例中感到震惊的对照是什么？
options: She was publicly unhappy but privately free from every difficulty.
Her public appearance of happiness concealed profound inner struggles.
Her friends all knew exactly how she felt at every moment.
Her difficulties were fully explained by one single social comparison.
optionsZh: 她公开表现不幸福，私下却没有任何困难。
公开呈现的幸福掩盖了深刻的内心挣扎。
朋友们每一刻都确切知道她的感受。
她的困难已由一次社会比较完整解释。
analyses: A 倒置了 appeared...happy 与 inner struggles 的关系。
B pretending to be happy in public 与 profound inner struggles 形成外表和内心的对照。
C 擅长呈现幸福不支持别人总知道真实感受。
D 前文强调复杂性及 many other things，不能归为单一原因，也不能由外表判断个体风险。

vocabulary.context: appeared 限定为外在印象，不代表没有内心困难或临床上的确定判断。
vocabulary.example: The character appears well adjusted at school but worries about fitting in.

questions.translation: 自杀是一种极其复杂的行为。Madison 的自杀，驱动因素一定不只是觉得自己的社交生活不如朋友，还包括许多其他事情。令人震惊的是，她如此善于在公众面前装作快乐；一个看上去适应良好、很幸福的人，也有深刻的内心挣扎，最终走向悲剧。她是例外，还是普遍情形？

evidence.quote: What is shocking is how good she was at pretending to be happy in public, and that a person who appeared so well adjusted and happy also had profound inner struggles leading to a tragic fate.

questions.passage: Suicide is an extremely complex behavior. Madison’s suicide must have been driven not just from feeling inferior to her friends’ social lives, but also from many other things. What is shocking is how good she was at pretending to be happy in public, and that a person who appeared so well adjusted and happy also had profound inner struggles leading to a tragic fate. Was she an exception or a rule?
questions.prompt: What does the question 'Was she an exception or a rule?' invite the reader to consider?
questions.promptZh: Was she an exception or a rule? 引导读者思考什么？
options: Which university rule Madison had broken.
Whether one case can establish the cause of every tragedy.
Why all people with similar appearances must feel the same.
Whether the case is unusual or reflects a more widespread pattern.
optionsZh: 麦迪逊违反了哪条校规。
一个案例是否能确定所有悲剧的原因。
为何外表相似的所有人都必然有相同感受。
这个案例是个别现象，还是反映较广泛的情形。
analyses: A rule 与 exception 对照指通常情形，不是校规。
B 问句关注是否常见，没有用个案建立普遍因果。
C 并未断言所有外表相似者感受相同。
D exception or a rule 对照个别与常态，以疑问转向普遍性问题；本身还未证明答案。

vocabulary.meaning: 常态；通常情况（此处不是规章）
vocabulary.context: 与 exception 配对，询问案例是否代表更常见的情况。
vocabulary.example: In this quiet town, a traffic jam is the exception rather than the rule.
collocations: the exception rather than the rule
